previous_statement: If f: |K| -> M is a homeomorphism onto a compact space M, then |K| is compact. The open stars st(v), over all vertices v of K, form an open cover of |K|: a point lies in the open star of every vertex having positive barycentric coordinate in its unique open simplex. Compactness gives a finite subcover st(v_1),...,st(v_N). A vertex w belongs to st(v) exactly when w=v, because w is the relative interior of the zero-simplex {w}; hence every vertex of K is among v_1,...,v_N, so K has finitely many vertices.
new_statement: If f: |K| -> M is a homeomorphism onto a compact space M, then |K| is compact. For each vertex v of K, define its open star st(v) as the union of the relative interiors of all simplices containing v. These stars cover |K| because every point lies in the relative interior of its unique support simplex and that simplex has a vertex. Each st(v) is open in the weak topology on |K|: its intersection with a simplex sigma is empty when v is not a vertex of sigma and is the relatively open set where the barycentric coordinate lambda_v is positive when v is a vertex of sigma. Compactness therefore gives a finite subcover st(v_1),...,st(v_N). A vertex w belongs to st(v) exactly when w=v, because w lies in the relative interior of the zero-simplex {w}; hence every vertex of K is among v_1,...,v_N, so K has finitely many vertices.
